native_retrieval.title: Delhi High Court Upholds Wife's Right to Maintenance Despite Inherited Assets | Amish Aggarwala posted on the topic | LinkedIn
native_retrieval.snippet: The ruling came while dealing with a petition filed by a husband challenging a trial court’s order directing him to pay ₹50,000 per month as interim maintenance to his wife under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act. The husband argued that since the wife owned inherited and family-gifted assets and came from a financially stable background, she had sufficient independent means and was not entitled to maintenance. The Delhi High Court held that a non-earning spouse, particularly a homemaker with no taxable income, cannot be compelled to produce Income Tax Returns to prove unemployment, observing that such a demand is “to demand the impossible.” Upholding a Family Court order granting interim maintenance of ₹25,000 per month each to the wife and daughter under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, the Court ruled that the absence of ITRs or detailed expense bills does not defeat the statutory right to maintenance when the husband’s income is admitted and substantial.
